title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio
abstract: Background: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient). Aims: We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment. Methods: Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell’s C-index. Results: Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001). Conclusions: Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. title: Liver Extracellular Volume in Patients With Tricuspid Regurgitation: A Novel Prognostic Marker
abstract: BACKGROUND: Liver extracellular volume (L-ECV), a novel cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) parameter of systemic venous congestion, might help to stratify tricuspid regurgitation (TR) patients at higher risk, but its role in this context is unexplored. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the incremental prognostic relevance of L-ECV in a large TR cohort. METHODS: Data were collected from patients with TR referred to CMR between 2019 and 2024 who had parametric mapping analysis for L-ECV quantification. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalization, under medical management. RESULTS: In 462 patients included (median age: 67 years; 43% female), median left ventricular ejection fraction was 51% (Q1-Q3: 40%-59%), median tricuspid regurgitant fraction was 21% (Q1-Q3: 14%-33%), and median L-ECV was 31% (Q1-Q3: 28%-35%). When dividing the cohort according to median L-ECV value, patients with high L-ECV (≥ median) showed worse baseline status with more clinical and imaging signs of right HF and (after a median follow-up of 2.1 years) poorer survival free from the primary outcome (P < 0.001) compared with patients with low L-ECV. High L-ECV independently predicted the outcome even after multivariable adjustment accounting for TR severity, biventricular ejection fraction, and pulmonary pressure (adjusted HR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.03-3.18; P = 0.030). Finally, L-ECV showed incremental prognostic value compared with TRI-SCORE when assessed in a nested Cox model. CONCLUSIONS: In our large real-world TR cohort, L-ECV appeared as a novel, powerful CMR marker of right HF with an independent and incremental prognostic value to stratify patients with TR at higher risk of events.

title: Right Atrial Phasic Function Improves CMR-Based Prognostication in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Study
abstract: AIMS: In multiple cardiovascular diseases, right atrial (RA) function can serve as an independent predictor for the clinical status and prognosis. However, the prognostic value of RA strain in patients with heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) remains considerably unknown. This study aims to explore the relationships between RA strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging-feature tracking (CMR-FT) and adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF. METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with HFmrEF who were referred for echocardiography and CMR at two tertiary medical centers from April 2016 to September 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, HF-related hospitalization and cardiac transplantation. The findings were validated in a cohort of patients with HFmrEF enrolled from two additional tertiary care centers (January 2019 to January 2025). The development cohort included 1317 patients, and the validation cohort comprised 385 patients. During a median follow-up period of 2.8 years and 2.1 years, respectively, 243 and 72 patients in the development cohort and validation cohort reached the primary endpoint, respectively. Cox regression analysis showed that RA conduit strain was an independent predictor of the primary outcome (HR: 0.86 [0.82, 0.90]; P < .001). The full model integrating clinical variables, traditional imaging, and RA strain achieved the best predictive performance (C-index: 0.80 in development, 0.81 in validation cohorts). CONCLUSION: RA conduit strain derived from CMR is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF, providing incremental prognostic value beyond traditional clinical and imaging-derived risk markers.​.

title: Prognostic Value of 13N-Ammonia PET–Derived Myocardial Flow Reserve and Its Association With Peripheral Arterial Flow Impairment and Aortic Stiffness in Hemodialysis Patients
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hemodialysis patients carry markedly elevated cardiovascular mortality risk, yet validated prognostic tools remain limited. We investigated whether 13N-ammonia PET-derived myocardial flow reserve (MFR) independently predicts all-cause mortality and whether upstroke time (UT) and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) are independent determinants of Global MFR. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 207 hemodialysis patients (median age 73 years, 65% male) who underwent 13N-ammonia PET between May 2013 and May 2024 (median follow-up 1,487 days). Prognostic value was assessed by multivariable Cox regression and incremental value indices. Determinants of Global MFR were evaluated by multivariable linear regression simultaneously adjusting for UT and baPWV. RESULTS: During follow-up, 100 patients (48%) died. Global MFR independently predicted all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 0.26, 95% CI 0.15–0.45, p < 0.001; C-statistic 0.724) with significant incremental value beyond clinical risk factors (ΔAUC +0.060, NRI +0.303, IDI +0.060; all p < 0.05). In multivariable linear regression (N = 196), both UT (β = −0.040 per 10 ms, p < 0.001) and baPWV (β = −0.015 per 100 cm/s, p = 0.006) were independent determinants of Global MFR (R2 = 0.236), despite being only weakly correlated (ρ = 0.069). Exploratory analyses showed stronger MFR associations with cardiovascular death (HR 0.195, p = 0.0008) than all-cause mortality. CONCLUSIONS: In hemodialysis patients, 13N-ammonia PET–derived Global MFR independently predicts all-cause mortality with incremental prognostic value beyond established risk factors. Both UT and baPWV are independently associated with lower Global MFR, suggesting that peripheral arterial flow impairment and aortic stiffness may each contribute to impaired coronary flow reserve.

Bivalirudin With a High-Dose Post-PCI Infusion Versus Heparin During Primary PCI in STEMI: One-Year Results From the BRIGHT-4 Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: The BRIGHT-4 trial (Bivalirudin With Prolonged Full-Dose Infusion During Primary PCI Versus Heparin Trial-4) demonstrated that procedural anticoagulation with bivalirudin plus a high-dose postprocedure infusion reduced the 30-day composite end point of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding compared with heparin monotherapy in patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with radial artery access. We now report the 12-month follow-up results to evaluate the long-term outcomes of primary PCI with these 2 anticoagulation regimens. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial, 6016 patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary PCI with radial artery access were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive bivalirudin with a high-dose post-PCI infusion for 2 to 4 hours (n=3009) or heparin monotherapy (n=3007). The primary outcome of interest was the composite of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding at 12 months. RESULTS: At 12 months, the primary outcome occurred in 124 (4.1%) patients in the bivalirudin group and 169 (5.6%) patients in the heparin group (hazard ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.58-0.92]; P=0.007). Bivalirudin resulted in lower 12-month rates of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding (0.6% versus 1.2%; hazard ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.28-0.87]; P=0.01) and stent thrombosis (0.8% versus 1.3%; hazard ratio, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.36-0.99]; P=0.045), with nonsignificant differences in all-cause death (3.8% versus 4.8%; hazard ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.63-1.02]; P=0.08), cardiovascular death, reinfarction, ischemia-driven target vessel revascularization, and stroke between the 2 groups. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary PCI with radial artery access, the benefits of bivalirudin with a high-dose post-PCI infusion in reducing the composite end point of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding at 30 days compared with heparin monotherapy are maintained through 12-month follow-up. These findings support the use of bivalirudin with a post-PCI high-dose infusion as an alternative to heparin to reduce mortality and major bleeding in patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03822975.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year. RESULTS: We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.66]; P=0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.47]; P < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04864145.

title: Sirolimus- Versus Everolimus-Eluting Stents With Contemporary PCI in Three-Vessel Disease: The Multivessel TALENT Randomized Noninferiority Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has improved outcomes in three-vessel disease (3VD). However, the Supraflex Cruz sirolimus-eluting stent (SES) has not been compared with the SYNERGY everolimus-eluting stent (EES) in this setting. OBJECTIVES: We compared the performance of the Supraflex Cruz SES and the SYNERGY EES in patients with de novo 3VD undergoing contemporary PCI. METHODS: We randomized 1,548 patients to the Supraflex Cruz SES (n=774) or the SYNERGY EES (n=774). Patients were selected after Heart Team discussion incorporating the SYNTAX Score II. Contemporary PCI included angiography-derived physiology, intravascular imaging optimization, CTO expertise, and short DAPT followed by prasugrel monotherapy. The primary endpoint was the 1-year patient-oriented composite endpoint (POCE: all-cause death, any stroke, any myocardial infarction, or any revascularization), estimated by Kaplan–Meier in the intention-to-treat population. The non-inferiority margin was 4.28%. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 367 days (IQR, 362–372). At 1 year, POCE was 15.23% (95% CI, 12.87–17.96) with Supraflex Cruz SES and 14.51% (95% CI, 12.20–17.21) with SYNERGY EES. The risk difference was 0.72 percentage points; the one-sided 95% upper confidence bound was 3.71%, below the margin (P non-inferiority=0.025). Myocardial infarction occurred in 10.07% (95% CI, 8.14–12.43) versus 8.14% (95% CI, 6.41–10.33), revascularization in 6.40% (95% CI, 4.86–8.40) versus 6.81% (95% CI, 5.22–8.87), and stent thrombosis in 1.31% (95% CI, 0.71–2.43) versus 1.08% (95% CI, 0.54–2.14). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with 3VD undergoing contemporary PCI, the Supraflex Cruz SES was noninferior to the SYNERGY EES for 1-year POCE. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT04390672

title: Spanish cardiac catheterization and interventional cardiology registry. 35th official report of the Interventional Cardiology Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (1990-2025)
abstract: Introduction and objectives This report presents the 2025 activity of the Interventional Cardiology Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (ACI-SEC). Methods All interventional cardiology laboratories in Spain were invited to complete an online survey. Data were analyzed by an external company and subsequently reviewed and presented by the ACI-SEC board. Results A total of 125 hospitals participated, compared with 118 in the previous year. The number of diagnostic procedures and coronary angiograms increased by 4% and 4.5%, respectively, both reaching record highs. Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) increased by 3.3%. The trend toward lower relative stent use was confirmed, with a marked increase in the use of drug-coated balloons, both as a standalone strategy and as part of hybrid strategies. The use of intracoronary imaging and coronary physiology techniques increased, reaching record absolute numbers. Interventional treatment of myocardial infarction increased by 3.6%, with primary PCI accounting for 98% of procedures. Structural heart interventions continued to expand: transcatheter aortic valve implantation (+10.1%), percutaneous mitral interventions (+25.2%), tricuspid interventions (+7.9%), and left atrial appendage closure (+8.4%). Renal denervation procedures, interventional treatment of acute pulmonary embolism, and interventions for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension increased significantly. Conclusions The 2025 Spanish cardiac catheterization and interventional cardiology registry shows overall growth in both coronary and structural activity. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

title: Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function: The LEAP-Block Randomized Clinical Trial
abstract: IMPORTANCE: For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed. OBJECTIVE: To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%). DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications. RESULTS: The primary analysis included 482 patients (LBBAP, n = 242; RVP, n = 240; mean age, 67 years; 46% female). Acute procedure success was comparable between the 2 groups (LBBAP, 237/242 [97.9%] vs RVP, 239/240 [99.6%]; P = .22), with left bundle-branch capture confirmed in 188 of 236 patients (79.7%). LBBAP significantly reduced the primary end point vs RVP (2.4% vs 12.5%, respectively; absolute risk difference, -10.1% [95% CI, -16.8% to -3.4%]; P = .003). Among secondary outcomes, the LBBAP group had fewer HF events (3.4% vs 11.3%; -7.9% [95% CI, -13.0% to -2.8%]). No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). LBBAP superiority was consistent across all prespecified subgroups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among patients with atrioventricular block and preserved LVEF requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, LBBAP was superior to RVP in reducing the risk of the composite end point of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials
abstract: BACKGROUND: Emergence of direct oral anticoagulants as the first-line therapy for stroke prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation has redefined the comparator benchmark for left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO). OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to compare the efficacy and temporal safety of LAAO vs oral anticoagulation (OAC). METHODS: Randomized trials of LAAO vs OAC in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation were pooled for incidence rate ratios (IRRs) per patient-year; key endpoints were assessed with trial sequential analysis (TSA) and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). RESULTS: Across 6 trials (N = 7,004), LAAO vs OAC was associated with higher ischemic stroke (130 vs 76 events; IRR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.07-1.91; P = 0.01; number needed to harm: 101; GRADE: low); however, this was sensitive to individual trial exclusion and TSA indicated insufficient information (41% of required size). All-cause stroke (152 vs 114; IRR: 1.11; 95% CI: 0.86-1.43; P = 0.43) and all-cause mortality (403 vs 368; IRR: 0.93; 95% CI: 0.78-1.10; P = 0.39) were comparable. Total major bleeding did not differ (IRR: 0.91; P = 0.29), but LAAO significantly reduced nonprocedural major bleeding (194 vs 232; IRR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.55-0.91; P = 0.01; number needed to treat: 19; GRADE: high) and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (145 vs 303; IRR: 0.48; 95% CI: 0.39-0.58; P < 0.001; number needed to treat: 15). CONCLUSIONS: LAAO significantly reduces nonprocedural major bleeding (TSA-confirmed) and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding vs OAC. A trend toward higher ischemic stroke was not TSA-confirmed and was sensitive to trial exclusion; all-cause stroke and mortality were similar. These findings quantify the benefit-harm tradeoff central to LAAO decisions.

title: 1-Year Safety and Effectiveness of a Next-Generation Dual-Seal Left Atrial Appendage Occluder
abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a stroke prevention alternative for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) intolerant to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC). The next-generation dual-seal device was designed to improve operator ease of use while maintaining effective LAAO of the predicate device. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this analysis was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a next-generation device through 1 year. METHODS: VERITAS is a single-arm, prospective, global, multicenter study. Patients with nonvalvular AF with an increased thromboembolism risk seeking a nonpharmacologic alternative to OAC were enrolled. One-year descriptive endpoints are provided, including mortality, neurological events, major bleeding, and device-related complications. One-year cardiac imaging was assessed for peridevice leak and device-related thrombus (DRT). RESULTS: Complete left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (0 mm leak) was observed in 91.1% (95% CI: 87.9%-93.7%) of patients by either transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac computed tomography and 96.3% (95% CI: 93.2%-98.2%) by TEE alone. The cumulative DRT rate was 3.3% (95% CI: 2.0%-5.3%) with only 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1%-1.5%) deemed clinically relevant. One-year key clinical outcome rates are as follows: all-cause mortality: 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4%-6.3%); cardiovascular mortality: 1.9% (95% CI: 0.9%-3.8%); major bleeding: 6.6% (95% CI: 4.5%-9.2%); ischemic stroke or systemic embolism: 1.8% (95% CI: 0.8%-3.3%); pericardial effusion requiring intervention: 0.9% (95% CI: 0.3%-2.1%). No (0%) device embolization occurred. Median follow-up was 365 days (IQR: 349-380 days). CONCLUSIONS: The VERITAS study results support the 1-year safety and effectiveness of the next-generation device. (Abbott Medical-VERITAS Study; NCT06707688)

title: Pulsed field, cryoballoon or radiofrequency catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) exhibit suboptimal outcomes after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. OBJECTIVE: We sought to compare the efficacy, safety and long-term outcomes of pulsed field ablation (PFA), cryoballoon (CB) and radiofrequency (RF) ablation for AF in HCM. METHODS: Patients with HCM undergoing de novo AF ablation were retrospectively included from 11 centers. Procedure characteristics, safety endpoints and 24-month outcomes were assessed. The primary endpoint was atrial arrhythmia recurrence (AF/atrial tachycardia). RESULTS: A total of 364 patients with HCM (61.7±11.1 years, 74.5% male, 47.5% paroxysmal AF) underwent AF ablation with PFA (n=84), CB (n=50) or RF (n=230). Procedure-related complications occurred in 1.2%, 4.0% and 5.2% with PFA, CB and RF, respectively (p=0.344). Cumulative 24-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence was 48.6%. PFA was associated with reduced atrial arrhythmia recurrence compared with RF (adjusted HR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.36-0.91; p=0.018), while CB showed no significant difference with either group (adjusted HR versus RF, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.42-1.21; p=0.212). In exploratory secondary analyses, PFA was associated with reduced cardiovascular hospitalization (adjusted HR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.23-0.80; p=0.008), and greater improvement in NYHA class compared with RF (p=0.032), while CB showed no significant difference. Heart failure hospitalization, repeat ablation, ventricular arrhythmias, stroke/transient ischemic attack and mortality did not differ significantly between ablation modalities. CONCLUSION: PFA for catheter ablation of AF in HCM was associated with reduced 24-month atrial arrhythmia recurrence, with exploratory signals of fewer cardiovascular hospitalizations and improved NYHA class compared with RF, while CB showed no significant difference.

title: Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery. METHODS: In this single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound-guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge. RESULTS: A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention-to-treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46-2.15], adjusted P=0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross-clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06-0.80]; adjusted P=0.022), lower postoperative high-sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: -2562 ng/L [95% CI, -4301 to -45]; P=0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06-0.98]; adjusted P=0.046). CONCLUSIONS: While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high-sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury.
